elements.evidence: Rendered § 12.4 now reads "Customer is subject to no restriction on soliciting, hiring, or employing any Vendor employee." The prohibitory operator ("shall not solicit, hire, or employ"), the term-plus-24-month duration and the "regardless of how the employee applies" no-hire tail are gone, leaving no restriction on Customer anywhere in the cited text, and § 12.3 independently confirms Customer has made no no-hire commitment.

No non-solicitation obligation of any kind survives in the rendered language, so there is no reciprocal Vendor-side restriction; the fallback's mutual-covenant construct is simply absent (the fallback is only offered in the margin comment, which is not operative).

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: there is no operative restriction left to scope, so no over-broad "any Vendor employee" coverage remains.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the term-plus-24-month duration was deleted and no restriction period remains.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with no restriction, no carve-out is needed; § 12.3 also expressly preserves hiring of persons responding to general recruitment.

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the "regardless of how the employee applies" language that captured unsolicited applicants is removed and no restriction remains.

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the "hire, or employ" prohibition is deleted, so no no-hire covenant binds Customer.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the single operative element — no non-solicitation restriction on Customer — is met by the rewritten § 12.4, which states affirmatively that Customer is subject to no soliciting/hiring/employing restriction.
Fallback is incomplete only because no mutual restriction exists; that is immaterial since the higher preferred level is fully met.

Minimality holds: the edit is confined to § 12.4 (the sole non-solicit in the document), converting the prohibition into a no-restriction statement without adding survival tails, procedures, expense language, or any requirement outside the checklist. § 12.3 and all surrounding language are untouched.

Intent is preserved and an existing inconsistency is cured: the deleted no-hire covenant directly contradicted § 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer has made no no-hire commitment and may hire persons responding to general recruitment. No undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or orphaned duration is left behind, and no Customer-favourable language was removed.

Drafting note (not a defect): if the counterparty resists outright removal, the cleaner alternative is simply to strike § 12.4 in full rather than retain an affirmative no-restriction sentence; either form satisfies the preferred element.
